title: Non-Abelian Thouless pumping based on the global adiabatic criterion in Rydberg synthetic lattices
authors: Jin-Kang Guo, Jin-Lei Wu, Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract: We study a quantum implementation of non-Abelian Thouless pumping in Lieb lattices using Rydberg synthetic dimensions. The lattice is encoded in twelve selected microwave-coupled Rydberg levels, forming a three-cell structure with six degenerate zero-energy states. These zero-energy states define the working subspace for cyclic modulation of the microwave couplings, while the remaining bright states provide the dominant leakage channels at finite evolution time. To choose the relative timing of the Gaussian pulses, we introduce a global adiabatic criterion (GAC), which evaluates the mean value and temporal fluctuation of a nonadiabatic factor obtained from a representative $Λ$-type transfer paradigm. With the resulting timing applied to the full twelve-level pumping dynamics, composing two elementary pumping cycles in opposite temporal orders produces distinct projected population maps. It is exactly consistent with noncommuting matrix-valued adiabatic operations in the zero-energy subspace. We numerically simulate the non-Abelian Thouless pumping using the Lindblad master equation with state-dependent Rydberg loss and representative perturbations. The results show that the GAC-selected timing within the same Gaussian pulse family gives higher target-state population than two literature-adapted Gaussian pulse schedules over the simulated parameter ranges. This quantum implementation of non-Abelian Thouless pumping, enabled by the GAC, marks a major milestone in finite-time geometric control and paves the way for transformative applications in holonomic quantum computing with Rydberg synthetic lattices.
summary: The research demonstrates non-Abelian Thouless pumping using Rydberg synthetic lattices to realize order-dependent quantum operations. A novel Global Adiabatic Criterion (GAC) is introduced to optimize the relative timing of microwave pulses, significantly improving target state fidelity in finite time compared to existing methods. This work advances geometric control and holonomic computation in solid-state analogues.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing non-Abelian Thouless pumping, which is sensitive to operation order, while mitigating leakage errors inherent in finite-time quantum evolution.
main_result: The proposed Global Adiabatic Criterion (GAC) for pulse timing successfully guides the system to achieve higher target-state populations compared to literature schedules, confirming robust non-Abelian behavior.
method: The authors derive and apply a GAC based on bounding the nonadiabatic transition probability ($\epsilon$) using time-integrated nonadiabatic factors ($Q$ and $\sigma_Q^2$). Dynamics are simulated via the Lindblad master equation.
model_or_system: The system utilizes Rydberg synthetic lattices, encoding a three-cell Lieb lattice structure within microwave-coupled Rydberg levels. The dynamics are confined to a six-dimensional zero-energy subspace for pumping operations.
key_observables: Projected output state (sensitive to operation order), target-state population ($P_{tar}$), and the nonadiabatic transition probability ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: The relative timing of Gaussian microwave pulses, which is optimized by the GAC; finite evolution time $T$.
main_assumptions: The GAC provides a conservative upper bound on leakage, neglecting potential phase cancellations. The simulation incorporates state-dependent Rydberg loss.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure and zero-energy subspace (Fig. 1); show Gaussian pulse sequences for two pumping cycles ($P_1, P_2$) with different temporal orders (Fig. 2); detail the GAC derivation using nonadiabatic factors $Q$ and $\sigma^2_Q$ (Fig. 3); and compare time-resolved populations showing order dependence (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model (Rydberg lattice, zero-energy subspace) and the pumping mechanism. It then introduces the GAC theory to manage finite-time leakage. Finally, it simulates the full dynamics using the Lindblad equation, comparing GAC-optimized schedules against standard ones.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the practical limitations of adiabatic quantum control by providing a rigorous criterion (GAC) for optimizing pulse timing in complex open systems like Rydberg arrays, which is crucial for realizing robust topological quantum gates.
